sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Western Balkans 6. North Macedonia Country Compendium
sources.temporal_coverage: October 2024 compendium; municipal vulnerability inputs include 2021 census and 2020 market-access data, with climate and economic projections to 2050.
sources.methodology: CCDR with climate-risk modeling, sector analysis and municipal hazard/vulnerability mapping.
sources.limitations: Municipal inputs are dated; impact modeling has significant uncertainty.

sources.title: North Macedonia Common Country Analysis for the 2021–2025 United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework
sources.organization: United Nations Country Team in North Macedonia
sources.temporal_coverage: CCA issued November 2020; analysis was conducted mainly November 2019–March 2020 and predates full COVID-19 assessment.
sources.methodology: UN country analysis using document review, interviews and participatory risk analysis.
sources.limitations: Mostly pre-COVID-19; dated national assessment, not a current local baseline.

sources.title: The Municipalities of the Republic of North Macedonia take steps to enter the 2030s with greater resilience
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, Regional Office for Europe and Central Asia
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports UNDRR cooperation and municipal resilience scorecards conducted in 2024.
sources.methodology: UNDRR report on city cooperation, scorecard workshops and disaster-resilience planning.
sources.limitations: Article summarizes the exercise; it publishes no municipality-level scores or measured outcome changes.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.81 (printed p.70), Annex C, Table C.1 and vulnerability methodology.
claims.paraphrase: Highest socioeconomic vulnerability ranks include Rankovce, Novaci, Staro Nagorichane, Pehchevo, Novo Selo, Plasnica, Debar, Gradsko, Berovo and Resen.
institutions: State Statistical Office of North Macedonia
claims.limitations: Index uses 2020–2021 inputs; not a 2026 update.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.81 (printed p.70), Annex C, Table C.1, flood/wildfire/landslide rows.
claims.paraphrase: High flood exposure: Aerodrom, Petrovec, Centar; wildfire: Makedonski Brod, Chashka; landslide: Centar Zhupa, Mavrovo i Rostushe, Debar and Tetovo.
claims.scenario: Flood: modeled 1% annual probability; other risks use hazard-grid averages.
claims.limitations: Modelled rankings, not event forecasts or observed losses.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.79 (printed p.67), Annex B, Figure B.1 note on modeled 2050 damages.
claims.paraphrase: Combined drought-to-crops, heat-to-labor and river-flood damages could reach 4% of GDP annually by 2050.
claims.scenario: RCP 4.5; maize/wheat, labor-productivity and riverine-flood channels.
claims.limitations: Lower-bound estimate with substantial data and compound-risk uncertainty.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.34–35 (printed pp.22–23), climate-shock response capacity and social protection assessment.
claims.paraphrase: Assistance can scale after disasters, but climate response lacks warning triggers and contingency finance; DRM law does not recognize social-protection capacity for displaced households.
institutions: Ministry of Labour and Social Policy
claims.limitations: Readiness assessment, not an event-response evaluation.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.33 (printed p.21), health system adaptation and climate-health workforce capacity.
claims.paraphrase: Health-worker migration, weak climate-health data and limited staffing impede emergency response; out-of-pocket costs restrict poorer households’ access.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.28, climate projections and subnational/group implications.
claims.paraphrase: CCA projects hotter, drier conditions and more extremes; southern areas face less water access and greater drought, wildfire and heat vulnerability.
claims.scenario: To 2100; magnitude depends on greenhouse-gas concentration.
institutions: United Nations Country Team in North Macedonia
claims.limitations: No southern municipalities or local scenarios named.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.28, climate impacts on agriculture and differential group vulnerability.
claims.paraphrase: Small farmers face water stress, crop and fodder losses; women bear disproportionate burdens in resource management and family care.
claims.scenario: Projections to 2100; yield impacts expected by 2050.
institutions: United Nations Country Team in North Macedonia

claims.locator: PDF physical p.45, interlinkages between environmental, social and economic dimensions.
claims.paraphrase: CCA places climate/environmental and demographic pressures alongside labor shortages, unemployment and emigration risks.
claims.scenario: Qualitative pathway; pressures and demographic change are not quantified.
institutions: United Nations Country Team in North Macedonia
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Climate/environment stress + demographic change -> labor shortage, unemployment, possible mass emigration; p.44.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.54–55, gender and climate vulnerability discussion.
claims.paraphrase: Women’s resource/information gaps and limited participation impede resilience; CCA also reports increased gender-based violence after disasters.
institutions: Ministry of Labour and Social Policy
claims.limitations: Violence is not disaggregated by disaster, place or period.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Disasters -> heightened gender-based violence; CCA p.55.

claims.locator: UNDRR report body, paragraphs on 2024 cooperation and scorecard workshops.
claims.paraphrase: In 2024 Gazi Baba, Gjorce Petrov and Ohrid joined MCR2030; scorecard workshops were used to establish resilience baselines and discuss local investment priorities.
claims.limitations: Article reports the assessment process; municipality scores and resulting investments are not published there.

claims.locator: UNDRR report body, description of scorecard purpose and national disaster-management support.
claims.paraphrase: UNDRR says the scorecard process identifies municipal resilience gaps and informs local strategies; it describes the national disaster-management system as established and expected to support municipal capacity.
claims.limitations: UNDRR describes expected support and planning intent, not tested resilience outcomes.

access_audit.notes: Cover identifies October 2024 World Bank Group country compendium; Appendix C uses municipal indicators and hazard grids.
access_audit.reuse_terms: World Bank copyright notice allows noncommercial reproduction with attribution and any required further permissions.

access_audit.notes: Cover dates report November 2020; methods section says analysis was conducted November 2019–March 2020 and most analysis predates the pandemic.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No reuse terms identified in inspected document.

access_audit.notes: Article dated 30 July 2024. It links an English-translated scorecard report but the article text itself supports the claims used here.

search_audit.query: North Macedonia national climate vulnerability assessment climate change districts municipalities flood drought official report PDF
search_audit.outcome: Opened the full World Bank 2024 CCDR compendium and identified named municipalities ranked for socioeconomic vulnerability and flood, wildfire and landslide exposure; the 2020 CCA adds southern-area and small-farmer vulnerabilities.

search_audit.query: North Macedonia climate change conflict mediator inter-ethnic violence climate risks report primary source
search_audit.outcome: The CCA links climate/environment pressures with labor-market strain and possible emigration, and separately reports disaster-related gender-based violence; no source-stated climate-to-interethnic-violence link was found.

search_audit.query: North Macedonia conflict fragility mobility climate adaptation official report municipalities
search_audit.outcome: The CCA records political instability and inter-ethnic tensions as national peace risks, but the reviewed primary texts do not establish violence or insecurity disrupting adaptation or disaster response.

search_audit.query: North Macedonia climate adaptation resilience capacity official report heatwave flood early warning municipalities World Bank PDF
search_audit.outcome: The CCDR identifies gaps in shock-responsive social protection and climate-health readiness; UNDRR records 2024 resilience-scorecard work in Gazi Baba, Gjorce Petrov and Ohrid.

gaps: The CCA and CCDR identify climate, disaster and social-cohesion risks but do not establish that climate hazards cause inter-ethnic tension, political violence or armed conflict.

The reviewed sources did not document violence or insecurity interrupting adaptation or disaster response; displacement appears as a function that disaster-risk and social-protection systems should address, not a measured climate displacement event.
The most detailed municipal rankings rely on 2020–2021 inputs; the 2020 CCA is pre-pandemic and provides few named southern municipalities.
UNDRR reports scorecard workshops and planning, but the article provides neither municipality-level scores nor verified investment or outcome changes.
